intro.heads_up: Quick heads-up before we dive in: by the time this episode drops Tuesday morning, WoW: Forever goes live that same afternoon, 3 p.m. Pacific in the Americas and just after midnight on Wednesday in Europe.
rundown: WoW: Forever going live worldwide, plus the beta by the numbers
a first look at Forever's roadmap and a four-month patch cadence
the name, layering and tuning fixes landing right before launch
a gold-buying ban wave that anyone selling carries needs to hear about
Midnight's Labyrinth fixes and 200,000 solo Kindo'jan kills
the Talebound demo and more housing on the 12.1.7 PTR
the Grimtide housing bundles and the backlash over Blizzard's shop promise
and we'll close out the news with Blizzard name-dropping Project Helix and WoW on whatever you want

items.title: WoW: Forever Goes Live November 4
items.synopsis: Forever goes live worldwide Tuesday at 3 p.m. Pacific, a permanent third game next to retail and Classic.
points: Blizzard's launch post landing October 29: November 4 at 3 p.m. PST, 12 a.m. CET on the 5th
set after Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom and before Molten Core, a full 1 to 60 journey
more than 1,000 new quests, with Mount Hyjal, Shen'dralas, the Riverglades and Zephras Isle to explore

points.text: the Skyborne debuting as the new race, Alliance or Horde, starting on Zephras Isle at 1 to 12
points.sub: Skyborne access requires the Heroic Pack or higher

points: new combos on day one: Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, Gnome Priest, Orc Mage, Troll Warlock, Undead Paladin
choosing a Classic or Enhanced preset before you even pick a ruleset, and HD or SD models per character
four rulesets at launch, Normal, PvP, Roleplay and Roleplay PvP, with Hardcore sometime after
the beta by the numbers: 8,862,354 characters created, 1,889,084 Skyborne, 612,096 Forsaken Paladins

points.text: the Kobold Miner crowned the beta's deadliest creature, and the Hall of Thanes its deadliest dungeon

points: a poster signing with the devs at the Irvine Improv on November 2, free tickets through TIXR
Jen and Eric's first Dwarf co-stream in over a year, November 6 at 6 p.m. Pacific, to celebrate launch
questions: Are we playing day one, and what's the race and class combo you're rolling first?
Do we have a guild plan for launch night, or is everyone leveling on their own schedule?

items.title: Forever's Roadmap: A Four-Month Patch Cadence
items.synopsis: Kris Zierhut tells IGN that Forever is aiming for about four months between patches, and the retail team wants Forever's lighting and water.
points: Kris Zierhut sitting down with IGN right before launch, with Wowhead pulling out the highlights
Forever aiming for roughly a four-month patch cadence
Zierhut also talking through where future patches could take us, and how respeccing works
the retail team confirmed to be talking about adopting Forever's lighting and water improvements

points.text: a very different pace from retail's eight-week patch cycle
points.sub: Windows Central called that retail pace "failing players" back on October 18

points: the first big beat already on the calendar: Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit and Onyxia's Lair on December 9
Blizzard framing Forever as a permanent home alongside modern and Classic WoW, not a limited-time mode
questions: Is four months between patches the right pace for Forever, or will people run out of things to do?
If retail takes Forever's lighting and water, what else should it borrow?

items.title: Names, Layers and Last-Minute Tuning
items.category: World of Warcraft: Forever, Pre-Launch Fixes
items.synopsis: Blizzard spent the last week before launch fixing name reservation and layering, and pushing one more round of class and racial tuning.
points: name reservation going live for NA and EU this week, after a delay

points.text: an overly restrictive name check blocking names it shouldn't, like anything containing "c-o-n"
points.sub: fixed with the next realm restarts, so if a name got rejected, try it again

points.text: Oceanic players on Australian servers hitting a ruleset bug
points.sub: make your Roleplay or RP-PvP characters first, or those rulesets disappear for later characters

points: forced world refreshes from layering getting significantly reduced
joining a group no longer auto-phasing you, as Blizzard works the top layering issues from beta
big talent tree changes for Druids and Paladins on October 30, after Hunter changes on October 28
racial tuning: Orc Blood Fury down to a 2-minute cooldown, Troll Berserking up to 15 seconds
Undead Touch of the Grave's internal cooldown cut to 15 seconds, from 25
Skyborne's Charged and Attuned buffs persisting through death, but removed when you enter a raid
questions: Did either of you get the names you wanted, or get caught by the restricted-name bug?
Do any of these racial or talent changes change what you're rolling on Tuesday?

items.title: Gold Transactions Must Be Direct
items.synopsis: Blizzard actioned accounts that bought RMT gold and had it routed through a middleman to pay for carries, and guilds selling carries can lose that gold.
points: Blizzard finishing a round of actions against accounts that spent real money on third-party gold
some buyers having the seller deliver the gold to a different player, who then sold them a raid carry
Blizzard's warning: gold from an intermediate player has an extremely high likelihood of being illicit
the rule going forward: always pay the player providing the carry directly

points.text: guilds selling carries at risk of having that gold removed
points.sub: when the buyer pays with gold that came from an intermediate

points: account suspensions on the table, on top of the gold removal
questions: Have either of you ever bought or sold a carry for gold, and does this make you think twice?
Is it fair to put the risk on the guild selling the carry when they can't see where the gold came from?

sources.label: Blizzard Forums: Gold Transactions Must Be Direct

items.title: Labyrinth Fixes and 200,000 Solo Kindo'jan Kills
items.synopsis: The October 27 tuning is live, the Labyrinths got another round of fixes, and over 200,000 players have soloed Kindo'jan.
points: the class tuning we previewed last week going live with maintenance on October 27, Subtlety rollback included
Labyrinth scenarios that weren't granting Great Vault credit, fixed October 27
Labyrinths now also dropping a Myth 2/6 item
the "Voices of Stone" bonus objective in "Bear's Burden" no longer getting stuck on the UI
Tether icons no longer flickering erratically in "The Wandering"
more than 200,000 players soloing Tier 11 Kindo'jan in two weeks
tabards no longer hiding the Rexxar armor set
PvP: San'layn Vampiric Strike down 20%, Devourer's Collapsing Star up 20%
and over in TBC Classic, heroic dungeon keys now only needing Honored, not Revered
questions: Have the Labyrinths been worth running for you now that most of the bugs are gone?
200,000 solo kills: did either of you get Kindo'jan down, and how many tries did it take?

items.title: Talebound Demo Live, Dornogal on the PTR
items.synopsis: The Talebound demo is open on the PTR with no subscription required, and 12.1.7 keeps adding housing to the Return to Dornogal patch.
points: the Talebound demo going live on the PTR October 30, no subscription required
the Red Hollow introduction plus three eerie tales across Normal, Veteran and Heroic
all three classes to try: Slayer, Inquisitor and Witch

points.text: Talebound's end-game rewards including Venomstones, bonus rolls and XP potions
points.sub: plus two pieces of Mythic Venomous Abyss loot and a Drust-themed hearthstone

points: Blizzard asking for feedback on the demo before it goes live
12.1.7 on the PTR with the "Returning to Dornogal" campaign
new cabin and theatre decor, and two new housing exterior customizations
questions: Are you going to try the Talebound demo, and which class are you starting with?
Mythic raid loot from Talebound: great for alts, or does it cheapen the raid?

items.title: Grimtide Bundles and the Hearthsteel Promise
items.synopsis: The new Grimtide housing bundles have players saying Blizzard broke its own rule against selling race-themed decor for real money.
points: the Haunted Grimtide Estate at $25: the Spirited Grimtide Manse exterior and Spirited Grimtide Foyer interior
the Grimtide Decor Pack at $10, 59 pieces from tentacles to a grand piano, on sale through December 1
players pointing out the pirate, Lovecraftian look is Kul Tiran-themed decor

points.text: Blizzard's November 2025 promise: housing items tied to the core fantasy of a race or class won't be sold in the shop
points.sub: Windows Central's headline: "WoW caught in a lie"

points: Bellular among the creators calling it out
the Living Heartsbane Cauldron mount hitting the shop the same day
and the November Trading Post going Sweet Tooth, with the Hot Motocross Bunmover 4600 as the Traveler's Log reward
questions: Is Kul Tiran-themed decor a real line being crossed, or does it not matter as long as it's cosmetic?
Would either of you pay $25 for a house exterior?

items.title: "On Whatever You Want": WoW and Project Helix
items.synopsis: Holly Longdale called Forever's gamepad support the first leg of playing WoW anywhere, and name-dropped Project Helix, the next Xbox.
points: GamesRadar+ asking Holly Longdale and Clay Stone whether a PC-only Forever is a missed opportunity
Longdale: "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want"
gamepad support as the first leg of that journey, and Forever as the perfect place to start
name-dropping Project Helix, and players already getting it running on the ROG Ally X

points.text: nothing confirmed, and Windows Central calls its own Xbox-port read pure speculation
points.sub: their comparison: Final Fantasy XIV got an Xbox port after more than a decade

points: a leaked email from Johanna Faries calling Blizzard Xbox's top-performing studio for FY26
Blizzard's third-highest year ever for top-line revenue, led by Diablo 4 and Overwatch
and the backdrop: Mike Ybarra saying an $1,800 next-gen Xbox "will never sell"
questions: Would WoW actually work on a console, and would either of you play it that way?
Is Forever the testbed for a console WoW, or is this just good gamepad support?
